content.title: Valerie Perrine, Oscar Nominee and “Superman” Actress, Dies at 82
content.text: Valerie Perrine in 2013Credit: Anne Cusack/Los Angeles Times via GettyNEED TO KNOWScreen actress Valerie Perrine died at age 82 on March 23The Oscar-nominated Lenny star was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease over 15 years ago, per a GoFundMe set up in her namePerrine was known for her work in Superman, Superman II, The Electric Horseman and moreValerie Perrine, known for her decades of work on the big and small screens, has died. She was 82.“It is with deep sadness that I share the heartbreaking news that Valerie has passed away,” wrote friend Stacey Souther in a Monday, March 23 Facebook post also shared on the actress' page.The Superman actress “faced Parkinson’s disease with incredible courage and compassion, never once complaining. She was a true inspiration who lived life to the fullest—and what a magnificent life it was. The world feels less beautiful without her in it.”Valerie Perrine in 1974Credit: GettyNever miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer​​, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories. Per Souther’s GoFundMe fundraiser shared in that post, Perrine “passed away peacefully at her home on March 23, 2026, surrounded by love, exactly as she had wished.” The “luminous, vivacious” Oscar nominee waged “a quiet, courageous battle against both Parkinson's disease and debilitating central tremors” for more than 15 years, it said.The fundraiser was “created with the full support and blessing of her brother, Ken Perrine, who himself continues to battle this devastating disease,” its description added.Perrine was born in Galveston, Texas, in 1943. Her father was in the U.S. Army, so the family moved around a lot. When she was 3, they moved to Japan. The family eventually returned to the United States, moving to Arizona. Perrine attended the University of Arizona for one year, then, as she told PEOPLE in 1974, "she ran off to Vegas, became a show girl. Mother cried, Daddy swore.”Valerie Perrine in 1982Credit: Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection via GettyShe became a star in the Lido de Paris review, performing topless in massive gowns with heavy jewels. “I pounded on every door 'til I got a job. And I got into acid for a while,” she told PEOPLE about her life in the city. She eventually left Vegas for Europe, where she “bummed around” before moving to Los Angeles.“[I] thought I better settle down and get a job doing something,” she told the Los Angeles Times in 2013. “I thought I could get a job doing commercials.” Instead, she was discovered by a casting director during a dinner party, and soon she was screen-testing for 1972’s Slaughterhouse-Five.“They told me to wear a bikini because they wanted to see what my body looked like. I didn’t have a bikini. I wore my G-string and that was it,” she told the Times. “I had been working in Vegas all the time and had been on the beach in St. Tropez, so being [naked] didn’t mean anything to me,” she explained, adding, “It was my attitude that sparked his interest and the way I read the line, ‘Oh, you’re a moon child.’ He hired me.”In 1974, she starred in director Bob Fosse’s Lenny Bruce biopic Lenny as the legendary comedian's wife Honey. Dustin Hoffman played Bruce. For her performance, she won best actress at the Cannes Film Festival and the BAFTA for most promising newcomer to leading film roles. She was also nominated for an Oscar.Valerie Perrine in Sweet Bird of YouthCredit: James Globus/NBCU Photo Bank“I swear to God, it's shocking to me,” she told The New York Times in 1974 of the acclaim she received for her performance. “I see other actresses, and they're brilliant, but I don't know what it is about me. . . . The biggest word I hear is vulnerability. Maybe I'm vulnerable as a person. But really, I do not know what is happening. I've never had any acting lessons.”Perrine’s early roles all involved her sexuality, which she said she didn’t mind. “The reason I don't mind is that I know I can act,” she told The New York Times, adding, "I don't care if I act as a sex symbol. Personally, I like sex, and I don't care what a man thinks of me, as long as I get what I want from him — which is usually sex.”“I don't think of myself as the typical sex symbol,” she added. “I'm not really beautiful, and my body is not perfect. . . . On the other hand, I am not dumb. I am not uneducated. I don't mind being thought of as a sex symbol as long as I have something else going for me.”Valerie PerrineCredit: Sam Levi/WireImageIn 1978’s Superman, she played Eve Teschmacher, the girlfriend of the villainous Lex Luthor. She reprised the role in 1980’s Superman II. Variety described her performance as “sensuous, yet almost innocent.” In 1981, she appeared on the cover of a Superman-themed issue of Playboy.Other roles for Perrine included 1976’s W.C. Fields and Me, 1979’s The Electric Horseman and 1982’s The Border. Her career stumbled after she appeared in 1980’s Can't Stop the Music, a movie inspired by the Village People. The film was so critically panned that it inspired the creation of the Razzie Awards — and she received a nomination for worst actress.She starred in the movie alongside Caitlyn Jenner. “Valerie was a lot of fun to work with,” Jenner told The Hollywood Reporter in 2023. “She would host glamorous parties for all of us, and she always had an army of beautiful women with her at these pool parties and lunches at her house. She was truly the hostess with the mostest and knew how to have a great time for us all.”Valerie PerrineCredit: Ralph Dominguez/MediaPunch via GettyPerrine starred in the 1986 comedy series Leo & Liz in Beverly Hills and made guest appearances on shows like Ghostwriter, Homicide: Life on the Street, ER, The Practice, Walker Texas, Ranger and Third Watch. She also appeared in more movies, typically in smaller roles, including 2000’s What Women Want.Perrine had a handful of high profile romances, including a relationship with hairstylist Jay Sebring, who was murdered in 1969 along with Sharon Tate by the Manson family at a dinner party Perrine was supposed to attend. She was also linked to famous men like Elliott Gould and Dodi Fayed, as well as some of her costars, including Jeff Bridges, with whom she starred in The Last American Hero. But they parted ways after filming ended. “I just don’t understand people in show biz. It really bugs me. You are so close when you work together, and then it ends, and so does the friendship,” she told PEOPLE in 1974.Perrine was diagnosed with Parkinson’s in 2015. Stacey Souther directed a 2022 documentary, Valerie, about the actress’ career and her life living with the disease. Souther was also Perrine’s close friend.“Valerie inspired me,” Souther told Parkinson’s Life in 2022. “She was a showgirl in Vegas during its golden era and a movie star in 1970s Hollywood during the last decade of glitz, glamour and excess.”“This film is a love letter to her,” he explained. “I didn’t want her to be forgotten. I wanted her life and legacy to be celebrated and shared with the world.”Read the original article on People
